title: Personal-data-shaped values under a credential-only scope
summary: Ordinary text containing synthetic personal-data-shaped values (a person's name, an address on the reserved example.invalid domain, a telephone number in the fictional 555-0100 range) and no credential, evaluated under a credential-only scope.
rationale: Personal data and credentials are different populations with different expectations. Under a credential-only scope these values are distractors: they test whether a credential finding fires on an email address, a name or a phone number. They say nothing about whether personal data should be masked, which is a separate profile and population that this repository does not define here. Mixing the two would let a personal-data profile's findings be scored as credential false positives, or a credential-only run be read as personal-data coverage.
unscopedReason: The input holds no credential of any family; the values are personal-data-shaped distractors for the credential scope.

expectation.rationale: Not flagged as a credential. This is a scope statement: the maintainer direction in issue #98 keeps personal-data expectations in a separate population or profile and uses these inputs only to test credential scope. It states no personal-data expectation. A record of the deciding maintainer and a second reviewer who is not the author is not made by this change and is listed under Needs human; until then the class is a labelled draft policy, not a fact.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed.
